text: The lab results show a total bilirubin of 7 mg/dL with a normal direct bilirubin of 0.6 mg/dL and low reticulocytes, which suggests unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia rather than liver obstruction or hemolysis. Since I have already requested an abdominal ultrasound to rule out anatomical issues, I need to know if the baby has passed meconium within the first 24 hours of life.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Late-onset). The clinical picture of a 5-day-old exclusively breastfed term infant with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (7 mg/dL) and normal reticulocytes is classic for insufficient intake or dehydration, rather than hemolysis or biliary obstruction. Please ensure the infant is fed every 2–3 hours to increase stool frequency and bilirubin excretion.
